checks: The tangentially tilted support at a nonexposed extreme point has all limiting maximizers at the desired endpoint. At each differentiability point of the scalar support function the tangential coordinate is its derivative; the support equality fixes the independent normal coordinate, hence there is a unique exposed maximizer.

In a positive-area cell with no exposed K point, every extreme point of K∩cl R is on a wall: otherwise a short subsegment in the open cell identifies it as extreme for K and density gives an exposed point in R. Each wall contributes at most two endpoints. The resulting polygon has nonwall facets on genuine support lines of K, because local equality in the open cell and convexity extend the supporting side to all of K.

For a zero-area open cell, a K point in it would force interior area; hence separation is valid. Its weak separating inequality on the open cell is necessarily strict there, so one containing halfplane makes that cell exact. For positive cells without exposed points, adding the nonwall facet halfplanes makes their interiors exactly match the clipped polygon.

Finite support approximations with fixed bounding directions give circumscribed polygons converging to K. Intersect with the finitely many exact-cell halfplanes and then apply the exposed-cell truncation parent to the other cells. The arrangement lines are null, so equality holds for all original halfplanes and the total.

dependencies.hypotheses: Apply in d=2 to outer polygons already exact on every cell without an exposed point and to the finite remaining exposed cells. Same-wave parent pending graph admission.

overlap.comparison: Its planar polygon approximation supports a mixed-area limit, not exact matching of an arbitrary finite line arrangement.
Its sectors are concurrent at one interior point with prescribed endpoint supports; it does not give arbitrary nonconcurrent arrangement cells with Hausdorff convergence.
